pr_title: run: when disconnected from PTY forwarder, exit event loop if not --wait
pr_body:
Follow-up for https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/ade0789fabbf01b95bf54d32f8cab1217a753f03

The change in behavior was partly intentional, as I think if both `--wait` and `--pty` are used, manually disconnecting from PTY forwarder should not result in systemd-run exiting with "Finished with ..." log. But we should check for `--wait` here.

Closes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/32953

review_comments:
well, the question is whether ^[ should be considered just "end pty forwarding" or be more treated like a ^C that hits the client, i.e. asks for program termination.

But I guess it's OK to declare that it should just end the pty forwarding, as long as ^C is then available to propelry kill the client at that point (and I think that works, right?) 

But can you add a comment to the sources here? i.e. explain this all: "If --wait is specified we'll only exit the pty fowarding, but will continue to wait for the service to end. If the user hits ^C we'll exit too."

(i mean, ideally we'd also output a friendly suggestion log message about this, but i don't see how we could make this reasonably pretty, given that most likely hitting ^[ results in an EOF/POLLHUP on the other side anyway which typically triggers termination anyway, hence any message suggesting to hit ^C is in 99.99% of all cases redundant and confusing)
Maybe better to mention that in the explanation of `--wait` in the man page?

let's do both ;-)

i.e. in both man page and in comment.
